algorithms.name: Epoch algorithm with truncated-mean score estimation
Cell-partition epoch algorithm with truncated means

symbols.L: upper bound on conditional noise densities
symbols.lambda_min: lower bound on smallest eigenvalue of E[x x^T]

conditions: contexts i.i.d., ||x_t|| <= 1, E[x x^T] >= lambda I
conditionally independent, centered noises with densities bounded by L >= 1
tuning: truncation level tau = (u n / log(dT))^{1/p}, u=(B+sigma_p)^p

source.label: thm:parametric
source.quote: Let $m(x) = x^\top \phi$, $\phi \in \R^d$ with $\|\phi\| \le B$ for a known bound $B > 0$. Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:density}--\ref{ass:moment} with full feedback, assuming $x_t$ are i.i.d.\ with $\|x_t\| \le 1$ a.s.\ and $\Sigma := \E[x_t x_t^\top] \succeq \lambda I_d$ for some $\lambda > 0$: the epoch algorithm ... achieves $R_T = \Otil(L\, d\, (B + \sigma_p)^2\, \lambda^{-2}\, T^{(2-p)/p})$

results.notes: Leading coefficient 196 L d (B+sigma_p)^2/lambda^2 per the proof. Regret is expected gain difference vs price m(x_t), recorded as pseudo-regret against the per-context optimal price.

conditions: bounded conditional densities (L), conditionally centered, independent noises
conditional p-th moment bounded by sigma_p^p
tuning: cell width h = T^{-(p-1)/(beta p + d(p-1))}

source.label: thm:nonparametric
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:density}--\ref{ass:smooth}, with $x_t$ having density $\ge \mu_0 > 0$ on $[0,1]^d$: the cell-partition epoch algorithm ... achieves $R_T = \Otil\!\left(T^{\;1 - 2\beta(p-1)/(\beta p + d(p-1))}\right)$.

results.notes: Problem constants (L, L_H, sigma_p, B_m, mu_0, d, beta) absorbed into Õ. At p=2 recovers T^{d/(2beta+d)}.

symbols.L: upper bound on conditional noise densities
symbols.lambda_min: lower bound on smallest eigenvalue of E[x x^T]

conditions: same conditions as Theorem 3.2 but p, sigma_p, B unknown

source.label: thm:adaptive
source.quote: Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:parametric} --- but with none of $(p, \sigma_p, B)$ known to the algorithm --- the median-of-means greedy algorithm ... whose inputs are $d$ and $T$ alone, satisfies, simultaneously for every $p \in (1,2)$, $\sigma_p > 0$, $B > 0$ and $\lambda > 0$: $R_T = \Otil(L\, d\, (B + \sigma_p)^2\, \lambda^{-2}\, T^{(2-p)/p})$

results.notes: Parameter-free; Corollary 3.8 restates this as no polynomial price of adaptivity.

symbols.L: upper bound on conditional noise densities
symbols.sigma_2: bound on conditional standard deviation (p=2 moment scale)
symbols.lambda_min: lower bound on smallest eigenvalue of E[x x^T]

conditions: Assumption 2.2 holds at p = 2 (conditional variances bounded by sigma_2^2, unknown to algorithm)

source.label: rem:p2
source.quote: under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:parametric} with Assumption~\ref{ass:moment} holding at $p = 2$ --- conditional variances bounded by $\sigma_2^2$, the bound unknown to the algorithm --- MoM-greedy, with inputs $(d, T)$ alone, achieves $R_T = \Otil\bigl(L\,d\,(B+\sigma_2)^2\,\lambda^{-2}\bigr)$: regret polylogarithmic in $T$, variance-blind.

results.notes: Polylogarithmic in T; Õ hides polylog factors. Setting s2 uses heavy_tailed noise; this result is at p=2 (finite variance).

conditions: no regularity of noise at zero assumed
tuning: median-of-means blocks k_T' = ceil(8 log(N^2 M_max T))

source.label: thm:adaptivenp
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:density}--\ref{ass:smooth}, with $x_t$ having density $\ge \mu_0 > 0$ on $[0,1]^d$, there is an algorithm with inputs $(d, T)$ alone ... achieving, simultaneously for all $p \in (1,2)$ and all $(\beta, L_H, \sigma_p, B_m)$ with $\beta > 0$: $R_T = \Otil(T^{1 - 2\beta(p-1)/(\beta p + d(p-1))})$

results.notes: Parameter-free in (p, beta, L_H, sigma_p, B_m).

symbols.L: upper bound on conditional noise densities

conditions: instances have context-dependent noise laws (fixed-support mixture), uniform contexts

source.label: prop:lower
source.quote: Fix parameters as in Theorem~\ref{thm:nonparametric} with $\beta \in (0,1]$ ..., and assume the mild nondegeneracy $(2L\sigma_p)^p \ge 8$. Then for every nonanticipating algorithm there are instances satisfying Assumptions~\ref{ass:density}--\ref{ass:regular} with these parameters on which $R_T = \Omega(T^{1 - 2\beta(p-1)/(\beta p + d(p-1))})$.

results.notes: Assouad + fixed-support mixture; holds for large T.

bound.regime: T large enough (depending on p, L, sigma_p, B)

symbols.L: upper bound on conditional noise densities

source.label: prop:paramlower
source.quote: Fix $p \in (1,2)$, $L \ge 1$, $\sigma_p$ with $(2L\sigma_p)^p \ge 8$, and $B > 0$. For $d = 1$, every nonanticipating algorithm admits instances of the parametric model of Theorem~\ref{thm:parametric} (with $\lambda = 1$) on which, for all $T$ large enough ..., $R_T \ge c(p)\,L\,\sigma_p^2\,T^{(2-p)/p}$, $c(p) > 0$.

source.label: prop:paramlower
source.quote: For fixed $d \ge 2$ the same $T$-rate holds with constants depending on $d$.

results.notes: Proof gives Omega_d(L sigma_p^2 (T/d)^{(2-p)/p}); dimension dependence not claimed optimal.
